title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Sonoma and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show winery, grape, AVA and vintage. Sonoma County is the broadest appellation; Russian River Valley, Dry Creek Valley or Alexander Valley are more specific. Single-vineyard names, like Rochioli or Bacigalupi, are common. US rules apply: 75% grape, 85% AVA, 95% vintage.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Russian River Pinot Noir suits salmon, duck, mushrooms and roast chicken. Chardonnay suits Dungeness crab, a local favourite, and lobster. Dry Creek Zinfandel suits barbecue, burgers and spicy sausages. Alexander Valley Cabernet suits steak. Serve Pinot at 14 to 16 degrees, Zinfandel at 16 to 17.
